definition: Learning classifier systems, or LCS, are a paradigm of rule-based machine learning methods that combine a discovery component (e.g.
details: typically a genetic algorithm in evolutionary computation) with a learning component (performing either supervised learning, reinforcement learning, or unsupervised learning). Learning classifier systems seek to identify a set of context-dependent rules that collectively store and apply knowledge in a piecewise manner in order to make predictions (e.g. behavior modeling, classification, data mining, regression, function approximation, or game strategy). This approach allows complex solution spaces to be broken up into smaller, simpler parts for the reinforcement learning that is inside artificial intelligence research. The founding concepts behind learning classifier systems came from attempts to model complex adaptive systems, using rule-based agents to form an artificial cognitive system (i.e. artificial intelligence).

explainer.lead: Learning classifier systems are rule-based machine learning methods combining a discovery component, typically a genetic algorithm, with a learning component. They matter because they identify context-dependent rules that store knowledge piecewise for prediction.

tiers.eli5: A population of if-then rules competes and evolves, and the rules that predict well survive and get refined over time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use LCS for classification, regression, data mining, and game strategy where interpretable rules help. A pitfall is tuning the evolutionary and learning components together, since the combined system has many interacting parameters.
tiers.paperLevel: An LCS pairs a discovery component (typically a genetic algorithm) with a learning component performing supervised, reinforcement, or unsupervised learning, seeking context-dependent rules applied piecewise. The approach targets complex solution spaces but is harder to analyze than single-paradigm learners.

explainer.example: In behavior modeling, a set of evolved rules each covers a context and predicts an action, with good rules reinforced over generations.
